Definition of done: root entry points direct agents to one canonical local skill; commands cover discovery, readiness, claims, bounded context, atomic changes, blockers and evidence-based completion. Remove conflicting Markdown-queue instructions. Merge the focused PR with required checks.

data.title: CI · Build desktop packages only for releases or selected manual platforms
data.body:
Goal: reduce Actions cost per user request. Own .github/workflows/desktop-packages.yml, docs/desktop-packages.md and this Ergo record as integration owner.
Source: S11 packaging maintenance; app-spec sections 2, 6, 10, 12. A-09/A-10 qualification remains open. No prerequisites or competing claims cover this scheduling change.
Done: published releases build all platforms; manual dispatch supports all or one of linux/macos/windows; PRs do not package apps; existing CI and concurrency remain. Merge focused PR after checks/review.

data.title: S16 · Headless Rootglass TUI and GPUI terminal bridge
data.body:
Goal: provide a headless-friendly Ratatui interface for Rootglass and embed that same interface in the existing GPUI app through a libghostty terminal surface.

This workstream follows the user's request to make Rootglass easier to exercise without a display, while retaining the ability to operate a booted guest interactively. “Feature parity” means the currently supported Rootglass workflows and the accepted v1 requirements: bundle open/import and verification, installed library management, trust and preflight reporting, run lifecycle, persistent state when S12.2 provides its service contract, and serial console input/output. It does not approve the explicitly deferred R3 features or turn unimplemented app-spec features into acceptance claims.

Architecture intent: add a reusable `rootglass tui` Ratatui application over `rootglass-app`; use Ratatui's `TestBackend` and a fake service for headless controller/render tests. Keep verification, trust, state, and lifecycle policy in shared application services rather than duplicating it in either UI. The GPUI frontend should host the same TUI in an embedded terminal backed by libghostty, rather than growing a second copy of the TUI. A compatibility spike must record the upstream libghostty API/ABI, pinned version, supported platforms, licensing, and packaging needs before shipping the bridge.

The workstream is complete only when the standalone TUI covers the agreed feature matrix, the GPUI app embeds it through libghostty, headless checks run without a display, and supported-host GUI/guest smoke evidence and maintainer review are recorded. Preserve existing security and release gates; reuse A-02, A-05, A-07, and A-08 evidence where applicable.

data.title: S16.1 · Define TUI parity contract and architecture
data.body:
Source: user request in the project conversation; docs/app-spec.md §§3–6, 9–10, 12–13; docs/roadmap.md. Read the current `rootglass-app`, CLI, and GPUI implementation before choosing ownership or duplicating a UI model.

Goal: make the new standalone and embedded TUI scope explicit and align the product docs before implementation.

Definition of done:
- Map current supported app/service workflows and applicable F-01–F-26 requirements to standalone TUI screens/actions, GPUI embedding, and headless/host validation. Mark service gaps and accepted limitations explicitly.
- Specify the `rootglass tui` entry point, shared service/controller boundary, terminal/PTY ownership, async operation semantics, and libghostty-to-GPUI integration contract.
- Update app-spec/architecture/roadmap with the Ratatui/TestBackend and libghostty direction; preserve R3 deferrals and distinguish implementation from release acceptance.
- Identify libghostty version/API, platform, licensing, and packaging questions for the prototype task; state which decisions need maintainer review.

Validation: verify every matrix row points to an existing API or a later task; check local links and `git diff --check`; have the maintainer review any platform or scope decision.

data.title: S16.2 · Build a headless-testable Ratatui controller and renderer
data.body:
Source: S13.1 `VTNG4C`; docs/app-spec.md §§5.3, 6.3, 9–10; S16.1 parity contract.

Goal: add the UI-independent TUI model and Ratatui rendering foundation without requiring a window server or real terminal.

Definition of done:
- Add a `rootglass-tui` library/module with a narrow service boundary around the existing `rootglass-app` APIs; reuse or extract lifecycle/action rules so the GPUI and TUI states cannot silently diverge.
- Render the core empty/loading/ready/blocked/failed/booting/running/stopping states with Ratatui and `TestBackend`.
- Test enabled actions, visible errors/corrections, selection, bounded output, cancellation/generation handling, and stale `RunId` events with deterministic fakes.
- Keep GPUI, a display server, QEMU, and terminal raw mode out of the headless model/render test path.

Validation: run focused `cargo fmt`, headless tests with `TestBackend`, and clippy for the new crate/module.

data.title: S16.3 · Implement library, verification, preflight, and lifecycle workflows in the TUI
data.body:
Source: S16.1 parity contract; docs/app-spec.md §§4.1–4.3, 5.3, 6.3; existing `rootglass-app` service APIs.

Goal: make normal Rootglass management usable from the standalone Ratatui interface.

Definition of done:
- Support opening directory-form and ZIP `.glass` bundles, importing verified archives, installed-release listing/filtering, reimport/update and removal, and detailed verification/trust/preflight/error presentation.
- Support boot, stop, and restart with explicit transition/action availability and actionable failure details. Never enable launch after an unverified result.
- Run file access, verification/import, and process lifecycle calls away from the TUI render/event loop; keep current operation and run IDs attached to completions.
- Exercise success and negative paths using the real service with temporary storage and a fake runtime/spawn boundary.

Validation: focused headless workflow tests prove invalid/untrusted/tampered input never reaches spawn and stale completions do not replace the selected bundle.

data.title: S16.4 · Add interactive guest serial console to the standalone TUI
data.body:
Source: S16.1 parity contract; docs/app-spec.md F-12–F-17, §5.3, A-07–A-08, §9.

Goal: allow users to interact with a booted guest from the Ratatui terminal, including sending login and shell commands over the real serial channel.

Definition of done:
- Display asynchronously batched `RuntimeEvent` output with preserved line breaks, safe ANSI/control-sequence handling, and bounded scrollback.
- Route keyboard input and Enter to the active guest serial stream; keep terminal controls, console input, logs, and focus behavior distinguishable.
- Reflect profile boot-ready evidence, unexpected exit, boot failure, stop/restart, cancellation, and stale-run events accurately.
- Restore the user's terminal mode and reap/stop owned guests on exit, cancellation, Ctrl-C, and errors.
- Cover split ANSI sequences, output floods, stale run IDs, input errors, cancellation and cleanup with headless/fake-service tests.

Validation: run the focused TUI/service tests and reuse applicable A-07 results; record which real-guest serial checks remain for host smoke.

data.title: S16.5 · Add state controls and trust diagnostics to TUI parity
data.body:
Source: S12.2 `6623ZQ`, S12.4 `UFT256`; docs/app-spec.md F-18–F-24, §§5.2–5.3, 7.1–7.2.

Goal: expose the supported state and publisher-trust workflows without creating TUI-only policy.

Definition of done:
- Use the state APIs and safety contract established by S12.2 to list/create/clone/select/reset/delete named state; confirm destructive actions and disable state changes/deletion while a guest owns the state.
- Show which state will be used on boot and preserve it across restart.
- Display the active trust configuration, trusted/revoked key status, and trust-loading errors according to the operations policy established by S12.4; do not expose private signing keys or invent a separate trust store.
- Test denied actions, confirmations, lock conflicts, trust errors, and the selected-state restart path.

Dependencies: requires S12.2 `6623ZQ` and S12.4 `UFT256`; also requires S16.3's core TUI screens.
Validation: focused tests with temporary state/trust stores; reuse A-05 and S12.4 evidence where it still applies.

data.title: S16.6 · Prototype libghostty embedding with pinned GPUI Kit
data.body:
Source: S13.1 `VTNG4C`; docs/app-spec.md §5 framework decision and S16.1 architecture contract; upstream libghostty public API documentation/source.

Goal: prove the requested embedded-terminal bridge is buildable and compatible before it becomes a shipping dependency.

Definition of done:
- Build a disposable GPUI Kit 0.9 prototype that embeds the supported upstream libghostty terminal surface and connects it to a PTY running a small Ratatui fixture.
- Demonstrate terminal output/control sequences, keyboard input, resize, copy/paste, and orderly child/PTY cleanup on an available host.
- Record exact upstream version/API/ABI, build/link steps, redistribution license, platform availability, packaging requirements, and CI strategy for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- Ask a maintainer to approve the supported platform set and dependency/licensing decision before the production bridge starts.
- If an upstream API or platform cannot satisfy this shape, document the concrete blocker and options; do not silently substitute a different terminal emulator.

Validation: reproducible prototype build and a short host smoke transcript; no product behavior or platform support is claimed by the spike.

data.title: S16.7 · Embed the standalone TUI in GPUI using libghostty
data.body:
Source: S16.3, S16.4, S16.6; docs/app-spec.md §§5, 6.3 and 10; maintainer-approved platform result from S16.6.

Goal: make the Ratatui application available inside the GPUI app through the embedded libghostty terminal, using the same AppService-backed behavior as standalone mode.

Definition of done:
- Integrate the approved libghostty terminal surface into the existing GPUI window and connect it to the `rootglass tui` session through the PTY/process contract from S16.1/S16.6.
- Verify interactive keyboard input, terminal focus and shortcuts, resize, selection/copy/paste, ANSI output, and PTY/process cleanup when the guest, TUI, or GPUI window exits.
- Keep security decisions, lifecycle transitions, state selection, and error rendering in shared service/TUI logic; do not shell out to an installed Ghostty app.
- Preserve the standalone TUI mode when GPUI or a display is unavailable.

Dependencies: requires S16.4 and S16.6.
Validation: PTY-backed tests with a deterministic Ratatui fixture plus supported-host GPUI smoke; record OS/CPU/build and limitations.

data.title: S16.9 · Add developer signing and package workflows to the TUI
data.body:
Source: S16.1 parity contract; docs/app-spec.md F-23/F-25/F-26; `rootglass-cli` sign/package commands; `rootglass-signature` public APIs.

Goal: expose Rootglass's existing signing and production-package workflows in the TUI without adding secret-handling risk or changing the signing format.

Definition of done:
- Add a clearly separated developer workflow for signing a `.glass` directory and producing a canonical `.glass` ZIP through `rootglass-signature` APIs, not a subprocess call to the CLI.
- Support the existing deterministic timestamp option; show publisher, key ID, signed-subject count, output path and verification result.
- Obtain signing keys only through an external secret file or supported agent handle. Never ask users to paste key bytes, retain key material in TUI state, or print it in errors/logs.
- Production packaging signs every regular file, including generated `.img` assets; the directory-fixture `.img` verification exception must not leak into this workflow.
- Cover missing/invalid keys, existing output, signing failure, package verification, and `.img` subject coverage with temporary fixtures and ephemeral test keys.
- Keep the current CLI commands supported and record any platform-specific secret picker limitation.

Validation: targeted `rootglass-signature` and TUI tests; verify output with the runtime verifier and confirm no private key bytes are logged or rendered.
